newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO FALLS AS SYDNEY SEEDS TUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO FALLS AS SYDNEY SEEDS TUMBLE.

text.p: Spain's Arantxa Sanchez Vicario was the most prominent victim of the day on Tuesday as the seeds tumbled out of the Sydney International tennis tournament.
Half of the 16 men's and women's seeds lost first-round matches including men's number two seed Wayne Ferreira of South Africa, beaten 2-6 6-0 6-3 by Spanish baseliner Carlos Moya.
Sanchez Vicario, world ranked number three and top seed in the women's draw, lost 6-3 6-3 to American Amy Frazier, ranked 33, in a match delayed by rain and hit by high summer winds.
The Spaniard said it was the first time she had been defeated in the first round of an event for which she was top seed.
"But I had an opponent who played better than me today and I probably made more errors than normal and that caused me to lose the match," she added

Other women seeds to go out of the tournament, which serves as a warm-up to next week's Australian Open in Melbourne, included seventh seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands and eighth seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa.
Coetzer lost 6-1 3-6 6-2 to Mary Joe Fernandez of the United States while Schultz-McCarthy lost 6-4 6-7 6-4 to Rachel McQuillan of Australia.

In other women's ties, former prodigy Jennifer Capriati looked in comeback mood as she defeated fellow American Chanda Rubin and Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia beat U.S.-based French star Mary Pierce in straight sets.

Capriati, 20, is a former title-holder in Sydney and showed flashes of her past brilliance as she downed Rubin 6-3 4-6 6-3. It was her first appearance in Australia for four years after a series of well-publicised off-court tribulations.
In the men's draw, five of the eight seeds tumbled out in the first round including number four seed Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands, beaten 6-4 2-6 6-1 by Mikael Tillstrom of Sweden.

Spain's Sergi Bruguera, French Open champion in 1993 and 1994, ousted compatriot Felix Mantilla, seeded five, 7-6 6-3, and Adrian Voinea of Romania beat seventh-seeded Petr Korda of the Czech Republic 7-6 6-3.
Switzerland's 1992 Olympic champion Marc Rosset, seeded number six, lost to Australian doubles specialist Todd Woodbridge 6-1 6-4.
